content: Urine antigen detection may not provide reliable diagnostic value for suspected disease caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) within one to two weeks following the administration of a Hib-containing vaccine, such as HIBERIX. In clinical studies, a booster dose of HIBERIX was administered concurrently with one of the following vaccines: DTaP, DTaP-IPV, DTaP-HBV-IPV, or DTaP-HBV (manufactured by GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals, which is not licensed in the United States). Additionally, HIBERIX was administered alongside U.S.-licensed vaccines such as INFANRIX, KINRIX, and PEDIARIX, each containing 5 mg of 2-phenoxyethanol per dose as a preservative. It is important to note that the dosing regimens for DTaP-IPV and DTaP-HBV-IPV used in these studies are not approved in the United States. Currently, there is insufficient data to confirm the absence of interference with immune responses to other vaccines administered concomitantly with HIBERIX. If HIBERIX is given at the same time as other injectable vaccines, they should be administered using separate syringes and at different injection sites. HIBERIX should not be mixed with any other vaccine in the same syringe or vial. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (when used in doses exceeding physiological levels), may diminish the immune response to HIBERIX.
